title: Retention administration and holds

acceptance.inventory: Current-session scoped source inventory with UTF-8 payload/receipt/history counts, protected identities, explicit holds and authorized-generation pagination. Trusted persisted source associations resolve ownership; browser scope grants nothing. Global source admission bounds include denied resources.
acceptance.review: Private source snapshots bind exact selection, source versions/counts, payload/history entries, policy/hold revision, cutoff and deletion bounds. Changed/forged previews fail; current authority is checked before new execution and retained receipt replay. Payload retirement and exact receipt commit atomically.
acceptance.imports: Durable holds preserve terminal raw source and superseded correction/history copies across preopened upgraded connections/restart. Reviewed purge replaces accepted result payloads with expired fingerprint identities; original correction/apply retries fail with IMPORT_OPERATION_EXPIRED and cannot execute again. Job/source identity and imported application values remain.
acceptance.collaboration: Holds suppress receipt/operation/source-history cleanup. Purge advances a persisted accepted-base floor while retaining current text, branches and their identities/history. Old edits conflict after receipt retirement; current-revision edits continue.
acceptance.audit: Pending/unsigned audit events cannot retire. Held acknowledged envelopes remain local without redelivery; bounded outbox growth applies backpressure and still delivers pending signed events. Retirement preserves sequence/checkpoints, independently verified continuity and other organizations. Invalid next events cannot starve already signed delivery.
acceptance.holds: Persisted, expiring and versioned; expired rows remain inspectable. Release/recreation cannot reuse a prior version. General database global/per-document history cleanup honors active source holds. A real 100,000-snapshot fixture proves capacity rollback keeps text, history and receipts intact.
acceptance.schedule: Persisted principal/session, policy revision, rule version, occurrence, cursor and next due time. Independent processes execute one occurrence; revocation or changed policy pauses it. Failed purge rolls back, errors remain bounded, missed cadences coalesce and cursor rotation avoids starvation by held early resources.
acceptance.recovery: Real SIGKILL after payload deletion and receipt insertion rolls back the complete SQLite boundary. Independent processes return one exact accepted purge. A deliberately lost committed HTTP response replays identically after service restart.

browser.transport: Actual same-origin HTTP handlers over disposable SQLite, persisted source metadata and operator roles; browser cookies and CSRF retained.
browser.rules: A paused browser-daily rule persisted through Save/Load; keyboard Edit restored its current version and focused Rule name.
browser.accountSwitch: Second real authenticated cookie/session saw zero resources; private reason and rule fields were empty. Return to original account showed retained identities.
browser.revocation: Deleting the persisted operator role produced access denial and cleared inventory/rules/forms.
browser.disposal: Disposed controls removed from the accessibility tree; late/disposal races also covered in focused UI regressions.
browser.screenshots: Viewed through browser tool output; no saved screenshot file is claimed.
browser.limits: The standalone widget is tested; existing platform dashboard/CLI do not automatically embed it. Browser testing does not certify Docker/XFS or physical erasure.

browserFixtureErrorResponse.reason: CodeQL flagged raw exception text in the disposable browser fixture; normal and failing real HTTP requests confirm the fixed response.

limits: No physical SQLite/WAL/PITR/backup/archive erasure or cross-database atomicity claim.
Current document text, branches, job/source metadata and compact retry identities remain; scoped source transfers require trusted hold reconciliation.
Upgrade all source writers; old binaries that ignore holds/floors or reject new metadata are unsupported. Historical restores require reconciliation before reopening sources.
Held source history is capped at 100,000 snapshots/128 MiB; accepted retention identities are never silently evicted. Lifetime receipt capacity applies backpressure.
General history pruning follows source holds, but direct trusted SQLite mutation remains outside the public contract.
Standalone operator widget and programmatic platform adapter; dashboard/CLI do not automatically mount it.
Three privileged-host cases remain skipped; Docker/XFS certification and dependent deployment features still require an explicitly disposable compatible host.

delivery.conclusion: All six checks completed successfully on the reviewed head. CodeQL reported no new alerts. Its corrected fixture thread is resolved; no change requests remain. Protected squash merge succeeded, its tree matches the reviewed head, and both checkouts were synchronized.
